one_liner: Ahead-of-time Ruby-subset-to-C compiler by Matz; README geomean 8.5x faster than CRuby 4.0.4 with YJIT.
what_it_does: Spinel is a single C binary that parses Ruby with libprism, infers static types across the whole program, emits one C file and calls the system cc to produce a standalone native executable that needs only libc and libm. It is not a drop-in interpreter: you compile a program (`spinel app.rb`, or the cargo-like `spin` project tool) instead of running `ruby app.rb`, and programs must stay inside a large but restricted Ruby subset (no eval, method_missing, runtime define_method, ObjectSpace, refinements or subclassing of builtin classes).
how_it_is_fast: Whole-program type inference to a fixpoint lets codegen use unboxed C ints, doubles and typed arrays (sp_IntArray, sp_FloatArray, sp_StrArray) and direct C calls instead of dynamic dispatch; polymorphic values fall back to tagged unions. Small immutable classes become stack-allocated value types, short methods are emitted static inline, and gcc -O2 then optimises the whole program (it even folds the pure fib call tree at build time). A generational size-class mark-and-sweep GC, NFA regexp engine and mruby-bigint are linked only when used, and --gc-sections strips the rest, so binaries start in about 0.8 ms.
when_to_use: CPU-bound Ruby scripts and CLI tools that stay inside the supported subset (numeric loops, arrays, hashes, strings, structs, blocks): the README shows 19-54x over YJIT on integer/float loops such as mandelbrot, matmul, sieve and partial_sums.
Shipping a Ruby program as a dependency-free native binary (or as generated C plus libspinel_rt.a) to Linux or macOS hosts without a Ruby install.
Short-lived command-line programs where CRuby's process startup dominates; Spinel binaries start in about 0.8 ms.
Parallel Ruby code: the threaded runtime runs Thread on an M:N work-stealing scheduler with no GVL (data races are the program's problem, as in JRuby/TruffleRuby).
when_not_to_use: Rails or gem-heavy applications that rely on eval, method_missing, runtime define_method/send, refinements, ObjectSpace or C extensions; these are refused at compile time (docs/limitations.md), and only community transpilers such as roundhouse bridge Rails.

Code that depends on exact CRuby semantics in corner cases: typed arrays raise TypeError on a mismatched store, integers are fixed-width and raise on overflow by default, and open issues include silent wrong results (#6179: a String appended to by a callee through send/proc/lambda is not seen by the caller; #7612: -2**63 read as nil).
Allocation-, IO- or hash-bound workloads, where the README's own margins over YJIT shrink to 3.1-4.9x (io_wordcount, csv_process, gcbench, binary_trees).
Native Windows (MinGW/MSVC unsupported; use WSL) or a toolchain without GCC extensions (__attribute__((cleanup)), inline assembly for fibers).
Teams that need a stable, reviewable codebase: issue #7033 (Oct 2026) reports 213,837 lines of C in src/ with a single 17,672-line emit_call_body function and asks the project to slow down.

integration.form: compiler binary (spinel) plus static runtime library libspinel_rt.a; output is a standalone executable or a single .c file
integration.dependencies: build: libprism (fetched by make deps, vendored in release tarballs), system gcc or clang; run time: libc and libm only (pthread when Thread is used); CRuby optional (test oracle, spinel diff)
integration.min_toolchain: gcc or clang with GCC extensions; exact minimum versions not documented (README benchmarks used gcc 13.3; CI runs ubuntu-latest gcc/clang and macos-latest clang)
integration.platforms: Linux x86-64 and arm64, macOS Intel and Apple Silicon; BSD expected but not in CI; Windows only via WSL
integration.thread_safety: Generated programs support true parallel Thread with Mutex/Queue/ConditionVariable over a stop-the-world GC; unsynchronized shared mutation is a data race (docs/thread.md per README)
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — runs unmodified Ruby only if it fits the supported subset, and you compile instead of interpret; CRuby is kept as the output oracle for tests

gotchas: Release builds do not nil-check an @ivar before a call: calling through an ivar that a setup/reset method has not yet assigned segfaults (SIGSEGV); only -g/--debug builds raise NoMethodError (docs/limitations.md, kept for a 10-20% optcarrot gain).

Startup-bound rows: bigint_fib (1000 additions), pidigits (27 digits), str_concat (10,240 appends), fasta (n=1000) and fannkuch finish in 5.7-9.2 ms under CRuby, which is about CRuby's own process startup, so their 4.6-6.8x ratios measure startup, not the workload. I recomputed the geomean without those five and the constant-folded fib row: 8.54x vs YJIT over 22 rows, so the headline still holds.

The headline geomean covers the 28 benchmarks in the README table; the repo has 61-62 benchmarks (bm_getivar, bm_send_bmethod, bm_object_new, bm_nbody, bm_micro_lisp, bm_sinatra_mini, bm_jekyll_lite and others are not in the table) and the selection is not explained. Spinel's compile time (spinel plus gcc) is excluded while YJIT's warm-up is inside each wall-clock cell.
Integer +, -, * raise on 64-bit overflow by default instead of promoting to Bignum; use --int-overflow=promote for CRuby semantics or wrap for speed.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Spinel over YJIT or TruffleRuby when the program fits the static subset and you want a small native binary with no Ruby runtime and roughly an order of magnitude more speed; stay on YJIT (drop-in, full compatibility) or TruffleRuby (full Ruby with peak JIT) for dynamic or gem-heavy code, and use Lightstorm only if you are already on mruby.
verified_claims_summary: First-party README tables (2026-09-17, spinel 74c8e0a4, gcc 13.3 at the driver's default -O2, unnamed 32-core Linux machine, mean of five perf stat runs) time 28 benchmark scripts as Spinel-compiled binaries against CRuby 4.0.4 with --disable-gems, with and without --yjit; the geomean is 8.51x vs YJIT and 15.21x vs the interpreter (recomputed from the rows). Excluding the five startup-bound rows and the constant-folded fib row leaves 8.54x vs YJIT and 16.35x vs the interpreter over 22 rows (derived from page data).
status_note: Very active (dated releases since 2026.09.12, commits and issues daily, 2.2k stars) and MIT-licensed, but young and fast-moving, with open silent-miscompile issues and a contributor-raised maintainability alarm; build it from source and run your program through `spinel diff` against CRuby before trusting it.
